sentences.text: Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned Advocates appearing for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are that:
On 28.04.2019 at about 4.30 PM., when deceased was proceeding towards his village on Kalaburagi-Sedam Ring Road on his motorcycle, near Railway bridge ring road,
Cruiser Jeep bearing Regn. No.KA-32/M-8420 belonged to respondent No.1 was being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner to endanger human life,
came from behind without control over vehicle and dashed to the deceased bike and caused accident, due to which he sustained grievous injuries, he was shifted to Basaveshwara Hospital, Kalaburagi, with the help of Ambulance but succumbed to the injuries on the next day.
It is further contended that prior to the accident deceased was doing centering work and earning Rs.20.000/- per month.
Due to his death, the petitioners have lost their beloved family member, who was the only earning member of the family.
Therefore, the claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.32,25,000/-.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the claimants and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as Exs.P-1 to P-15.
On the other hand, respondent No.2-Insurer did not adduce evidence, however, got marked insurance policy as Ex.R1.
8. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
9. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal awarded the compensation at Rs.19,83,750/-.

10. Insofar as liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal noticed the documents placed on record and held that, the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and therefore, fastened the liability on the respondents.
11. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and award, the claimants have filed the present appeal.

The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal committed an error in considering the income of the deceased.
He contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced.

He further contended that the Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation towards loss of consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- to each of the claimants as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NANU RAM

ALIAS CHUHRU RAM & OTHERS reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.
13.
The insurer of the offending vehicle on the other hand contended that the deceased was also negligent in the accident and therefore, the Tribunal ought to have proportionately fixed the liability.
14. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
15. In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2019, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.13,250/- p.m. as per chart.

In view of the law laid down by the Constitutional Bench of the Supreme Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, to the aforesaid amount, 40% has to be added on account of future prospects as the deceased was aged about 40 years.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income is considered as Rs.18,550/-.
Out of which, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th towards personal expenses and therefore, the monthly income comes to Rs.13,912.5 rounded off to Rs.13,913/- (Rs.18,550/- - Rs.4,637.5).

16. As on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged 40 years, as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA (SMT) & OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier applied to the age group of the deceased is '15', which is rightly taken by the Tribunal.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA (SMT) & OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.25,04,340/- (Rs.13,913/- x 12 x 15) on account of loss of dependency as against Rs.17,88,750/- awarded by the Tribunal.
17. In addition, the claimants are entitled to Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

18. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM & OTHERS reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, each of the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of consortium', which comes to Rs.2,40,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 6).
19.

sentences.text: Thus the claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.27,74,340/- as against Rs.19,83,750/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,90,590/-.
(a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award dated 07.01.2021 passed by the I Addl.

Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Kalaburagi, in MVC No.664/2019, is modified.

(c) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.27,74,340/- as against Rs.19,83,750/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
(d) The claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,60,590/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the - 10 - date of claim petition till the date of realization of amount.

(e) The Respondent No.2, Insurance  Company is directed to deposit the  enhanced compensation amount along with interest, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(f) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be  transferred to the Tribunal for disbursement to the claimants in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
(g) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
